It didn't really make much sense to me and that's why I finally provided my statement on the 10th of November, stating that I didn't wish to meet with the Prosecution and that whatever I had to say I was willing to say in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. But how was this presented to you? You're saying that -- you told us this morning that the investigator said very few people talked to both sides. Now, how was this presented to you in terms of: Would you like to meet the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I inquired whether that was customary at all and they told me: It's up to you to decide. Without any intention to avoid or evade things, I simply decided to contact only the Defence team and that I would share my knowledge with the Prosecution once I was here in the courtroom, in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you have any reasons why you wouldn't want to meet with representatives of the Prosecution prior to testifying?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To be honest, I don't have any special reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So had the Prosecutor contacted you for an interview, would you have refused?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes. But as I've already told you, I didn't have any special reasons for that. Personally, I find it rather odd. It doesn't make sense to talk to both sides at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm not going to ask you about your knowledge of the judicial system, but there's actually nothing odd about meeting counsel from either side, but I'll move on. Sir, you told us about your time in the army and I was curious to know: Do you have your military ID card or your military booklet?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you have it here with you today?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Nobody told me to bring it, which is why I don't have it. But, as soon as I return home, I can make a photocopy of the booklet and I can either fax it through or e-mail the copy to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I would appreciate that. I want to take you to your time in Kotor Varos in early 1992. First of all, it's not entirely clear to me when you joined the Kotor Varos Territorial Defence exactly.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was on the 8th or 9th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And are you telling us that up until that time you were not part of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have my war assignment in the Territorial Defence. My name was recorded in the Territorial Defence, but I was never called up. Nobody got in touch with me. And there was no need for me to be actively engaged before that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And up until the 8th or the 9th of June, what were you doing -- what were your activities?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a businessman. I had my shops, a chain of boutiques. It was a family business. I was a tradesman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. So if we were to look at your military booklet, this -- it would be reflected in your booklet that you were called up on the --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And until when did you remain within the Kotor Varos light brigade? I understand you were a member during 1992. Until when did you remain in this unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained in the unit until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you have a title, a role, a function?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was the commander of a platoon that provided logistic support.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this was the case from the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time I was a member of the Territorial Defence among those who stood guard locally. Only when the brigade was set up we were all transferred to that brigade. I believe that the brigade was established in late June, as far as I can remember, and from then on we were all under the command of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when you were working in the TO guarding buildings, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Gojko Stolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when you resumed your activities as part of the Kotor Varos light brigade, at that time who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the same person. When the brigade was established, Gojko Stolic became assistant commander for logistics. I continued acting as a platoon commander in logistics looking after the fleet of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, it is correct to say that the Kotor Varos Territorial Defence was transformed into what became the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the logical flow of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And are you aware of the strength of this brigade in terms of manpower?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the numerical strength. I think that there were some 300 to 400 men to start with, but, really, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And it is correct to say that the Kotor Varos light brigade was made of companies not battalions; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first there were both companies and battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, I understood that your eyesight has been affected, but I would like to show you a document which will appear on the screen before you. And if you have a hard time seeing it, please let us know and we can zoom into it. It's 65 ter 1651 at tab 4, please. Now, you will see the version in your language on the left side of the screen, I believe. Now, this is a document dated the 27th of May --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. This document is dated 27th of May, 1992, and it is issued by the 1st Krajina Corps Command. And as you can see, this is a document which was issued at the time for the purpose of establishing the structure of the 1st Krajina Corps. Now, on that first page you can see that there is a proposal in terms of the commander, his staff, his chief and his organisational unit. I would like to take you to a page 5 in the B/C/S version which is page 4 in the English version. Now, under number 3 can you see the title "units of the corps"? Can you see the title, number 3, "units of the corps"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you see that there are about a dozen combat units of that brigade. And if we scroll down a little bit in the B/C/S version and -- I'm sorry, go to the next page, please, in the B/C/S version only. Yes. You can see at numbers -- number 4 "establishment potential by municipalities," and I believe you can see Kotor Varos is listed there and in the English version you can see the title and we can also go to the next page in the English version, please. There we are. Now, do you see next to Kotor Varos: "1 light infantry brigade (formed by companies)"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now we also see a number of other light infantry brigades related to a number of municipalities. Now, if we scroll down a little bit to the middle of that page -- that's in the English version, sorry, you will have to go to the next page in -- hang on a second. No, bottom of the page in B/C/S. That's fine. Do you see the comment: "Current commanders of municipal Territorial Defence staffs would become commanders of the light infantry brigades"? We can see that note in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is exactly what happened to Mr. Mane Tepic; correct? He was the commander of the municipal TO and he became commander of the light infantry brigade; right? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: During the month of June, did you know who was --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise -- yes, go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: During the month of June, did you know who was the commander, your commander, your ultimate commander?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ultimate commander, I believe that that was Gojko Stolic. I don't remember that Tepic was commander. I don't remember, personally. All my contacts were with Mr. Stolic until the appointment of commander, or rather, I met with the brigade commander, Lieutenant-Colonel Novakovic, after I returned from detention. By then he was already a brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. In the B/C/S version could we go to the next page. We could leave it in the English; it's on the same page. Do you see the comment at the top of the page which says: "The light infantry brigades formed by battalions could be up to 1500 men strong, and those formed by companies could be up to 1.000 men strong"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you told us just a few minutes ago that in your estimate your brigade was made up of 3- or 400 men. Would you accept that your estimates are based on your knowledge only at the time and that the number could have been higher?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I believe that the brigade never had more than 500 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know how many companies your brigade had?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, as far as I know, the brigade had a company in Kotor Varos, a company in Vrbanjci, the Maslovare company, and the Grabovica company, four companies all together. During the war when it was organised into battalions, as far as I know and remember, it had three battalions with three companies each, nine all together. Following certain logic, one would be inclined to agree that it may have had a thousand men, but that was well into the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Were you aware that by the month of July there is also a company in the village of Liplje?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And that there was also one more company, an infantry company, in Vagani?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In Vagani.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vagani, um -- there was a unit up there but I don't think that it was a company. It was a smaller unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, finally, were you aware that your brigade had an - sorry- 82-millimetre mortar platoon?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in our brigade, for a long, long time there were 60-millimetre mortars. It was only after a long time we got 82-millimetre mortars. I'm not saying that what I know is correct, but I believe that I'm right. This is at least what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to move away from this document. I'd like to have it marked and admitted. I believe that it is a useful document which establishes the context of the creation of the VRS and the 1 KK and I believe that Your Honours would benefit from having this contextual document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to the admission of this document. I believe that the OTP during their case and during the examination of their witnesses could have introduced this document to one of their witnesses, for example, ST-179, who testified here during the Prosecution case. Moreover, we can see that this is just a proposal as to how things should look like. This witness does not know anything about the information contained in here and the proposed composition and the numerical strength of the brigade. Also, he didn't agree with my learned friend from the OTP about the command composition of the light assault brigades, as it should have been. I don't see that enough connection was established between the document and what the witness knows. He told us in the examination-in-chief what he knows and what he saw on the ground. I believe that this document contains far too much information and that the witness was not in a position to confirm any of this nor did he know much about the establishment of the 1st Krajina Corps. I repeat, we heard a lot of witnesses who could have testified to this effect. I repeat, the knowledge of this witness is rather limited. I apologise, I believe I misspoke when I mentioned the number of the witness. It was ST-197.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, like Mr. Aleksic, whereas the document appears ex facie to be of some relevance, it is, to my mind, surprising that it wasn't offered as part of the Prosecution case. Moreover -- as Mr. Aleksic -- do you accept what Mr. Aleksic suggests -- said that, in fact, it is a -- I confess I was not paying attention to that detail, but it was only a proposal, it was not the final version? If that was the case, why do we need it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I don't have any strong feelings about this document. I fount that it is a useful document in that the 1st Krajina Corps was able to assess the strengths that it had available to it. And, in and of itself, with regards to what Mr. Aleksic was saying, we do have another document to show the strength and the command positions in this witness's unit. I do agree that, in and of itself, this document is a proposal, and once again I don't have any strong feelings about it, Your Honours. The witness actually confirmed a lot of what is contained in this document. It is also correct that the witness was in a platoon, per se, and may have no knowledge of the document. But the document, I believe, speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we move on. It is not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you a document which is at tab 5; that is 65 ter 2340. Can you see the document on the left side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, as you can see this document is issued by the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade on the 8th of June, 1992, and it is, in fact, the appointment of Mr. Mane Tepic. And I believe you can confirm that this document is signed by your commander, Dusan Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but it seems completely illogical [Realtime transcript read in error "logical"] for Dusan Novakovic to sign such a document because the date is the 8th of June. At that time this brigade was not in existence. To my mind, this is a false document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The word is "illogical" in line 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, the previous document I showed you from the 1st Krajina Corps was from the 27th of May, about two weeks before the issuance of this document. And in that document, the 1st Krajina Corps was proposing the creation of the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade. Why would it be illogical two weeks later to see the appointment of Mr. Tepic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know why? Because, to my mind, the brigade still hadn't been set up in Kotor Varos. It was set up later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: When --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This may be a proposal or something at a higher level with which I'm not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you had never seen this document before; correct?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Looking at the document itself, do you have any reasons to believe that it would be wrong?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the date, the 8th of June. Because if memory serves me well, this brigade was established later. Before I was taken prisoner, that is, before the 5th of July I had never seen Mr. Novakovic commanding that brigade. I saw him for the first time when I was released. That's why it is illogical to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You do agree, however, that up until the month of July or August you had no contacts with Mr. Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That signature, have you seen this signature before?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on. Now, sir, we were discussing the issue of the strength of your unit, and I would like to show you a document issued by the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade which is P1787. And this document which you will see on your screen in a moment is dated the 23rd of July, 1992. Now, I'd like you to pay attention in a minute when it comes up to the units involved. Now, you can see it on your screen now. On the top left, it says "command of the LpBr." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 23rd of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. You see that. Can we go to the last page for a moment, both in English and B/C/S, please. And it is tab 17, I apologise. Do you see that at the bottom right-hand side of the document it says that it is signed for the commander by Captain Manojlo Tepic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I would ask that we go back to page 2, please. And in English that would be also page 2. In the B/C/S version I would like you to -- I would ask that we zoom into the bottom part or scroll down, please, yes. Section 5. Do you see the section entitled: "Tasks for subordinate units"? And under 5.1 you can see "the 1st Kotor Varos infantry company ..." you see that? If you like we could zoom in a little bit more in the bottom part, in the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really see it so well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see the title, number 5, "tasks for subordinate units." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me a moment, please. But this is late July already, which confirms what I said, that Novakovic joined the unit much later or maybe not even then -- oh, but, yes, yes, he was there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Can we go to the next page, please, in both English and B/C/S. Now, earlier and under 5.1 we saw the Kotor Varos infantry company. And here you can see under 5.2, and maybe a little bit lower, 5.3, a number of other --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- infantry companies, Pioneers Platoon under number -- yes. And if you go to the next page in the B/C/S version, under 5.4 you will see the Vrbanjci Infantry Company. You can see that at the bottom of the page in English. And if we then go to the next page in English, please. You can see under 5.5 the Maslovare Infantry Company. And then next page in B/C/S, please. Under 5.6 you can see the Liplje Infantry Company, and under 5.7 the Vagani Infantry Company --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Is this the same document as the one that was signed in late July?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Absolutely. This is the 23rd of July. And under 5.8 you can also see the 82-millimetre Mortar Platoon. And we can go to the next page in English for that. Now, sir, I understand that in the month of June you may not have been aware of the developments or how far the creation of this unit was -- how far -- you weren't creating this unit. But it appears already from mid- to late July, the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade was fully formed, and as we can see there are seven or eight units fully employed in combat activities. Now, would you agree with me that considering your position in the month of June it is possible that you were not aware of all this?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I most certainly wasn't aware, and in July still I was unaware. And upon my return from captivity, frankly speaking, I didn't really care much about the units or the establishment because my mental state was such that my -- my experiences from captivity were foremost on my mind and that's what was discussed with me. And the rest isn't anything I would have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, we can move away from this document. Now, again, I do realise that you were at the level of a platoon command. However, are you able to tell the Court what was the area of responsibility of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, it was the territory of Kotor Varos municipality. As the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina developed, the brigade was relocated several times so that it fought in the Posavina and on Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And are you aware that your brigade had a few forward command posts?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't have a few forward command posts. I only know of one forward command post at Jasen beneath Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know of a -- and I don't know if you're referring to the same. Did you know of a forward command post which was on Mount Borije?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sure that there was no forward command post there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like to show you a document marked Exhibit 2D133, which is, again, tab 16, please. And this time this document comes from the brigade group command. This is the operative group led by Lieutenant-Colonel Peulic. If you look on the top left it is dated the 16th of July, 1992, and it is being sent to the 1st Krajina Corps. Now, I'd like you to take -- to go to page 4 in the English version, and that would be, I believe, page 7 in e-court. On the document it's page 4, but in e-court I believe it's page 7 -- no, no, the English is page 4, sorry. Yes -- no, I meant in the B/C/S it's page -- there you go. Yes. Very well. Under 5.3, sir, you can see the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade is to organise and carry out combat operations in the territory of Kotor Varos. Now, if you look a little bit lower, just before number 6 where it says "fire support," just above that there's a sentence which says: "The KM," which is the command post, "is to be located in the Kotor Varos SJB building ..." you told us as much earlier today "... and the IKM," forward command post, "is to be prepared on Mount Borja in Krusevo Brdo village ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You personally had no knowledge of this forward command post, did you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's move on. Now, sir, you told us that after you were released the assignments that you were given were in logistics; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We have a working sheet of the Kotor Varos Light Infantry Brigade which is at tab 39; the 65 ter is 2348. That's not it. Just a second, please. Can we try again, 2348. There we go. Thank you. Very well. Now, you can see on the top of the document it says "working map, military post 7001 Kotor Varos," and then you see the commander of the brigade, Dusan Novakovic; chief of staff, Manojlo Tepic. You see the assistant chief for operations and training. And then if we go to the next page English, it's down the same page in B/C/S, can you see assistant command for logistics, Nenad Jerkovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Jerkovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you know when he was appointed to that position?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And what is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The document is not dated, unfortunately, and that's why I was going to ask you, based on your knowledge, whether you knew when Mr. Jerkovic was appointed. Putting that aside, do you recognise any of the other names on this document?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know several names here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you can see already on that first page that you have assistant commanders for Mr. Novakovic and a number of assistant commanders and commanders of platoons, commanders of companies, and perhaps in the B/C/S version we can move to the next page. You can see the continuation of that list, but in English we can go to page 3. We can see platoon commanders, company commanders, and so on. Now, sir, I accept that your name does not appear on this document because they don't have it down to every member of this unit, but we can see quite a large unit here. From your understanding of the brigade command structure, would this reflect the situation in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way the brigade could have been this size in 1992, with such a large number of officers. This must be a later document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you see on this page at the top you have Gojko Stolic, who you mentioned earlier before?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It says that he is the commander -- yes --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vagani company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a surprise because I don't remember him ever being a member of the Vagani company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So this document itself -- you had never seen this document, and is it quite possible that you're not aware of the structure of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in principle, that's correct, I was not aware. I knew the people closest to me and I had very little knowledge about things out there in the field. Is this the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: There's one more page. We can move to the last page, which is page 3 in the B/C/S. And you can see it was signed by Mr. Novakovic. And, to your knowledge, Mr. Novakovic was replaced by another commander by the name of Ubiparip in 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third -- or rather --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's possible that he arrived in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And would you agree that this document establishes the structure of the brigade in 1992?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Seeing that --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. This document mentions the commander of a recruit platoon. Never heard of that. Commander of the logistics platoon Asim Aganbegovic. I don't think he was commander of the logistics platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And two rows below him is the person you mentioned earlier before, Mr. Adis Hadziselimovic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And to the right of his name we cannot see his ethnic group, although for all of them, we see Serb or Yugoslav?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, a Muslim. But I'm surprised by him being the deputy commander of the SPDV platoon. He fought together with us. Unfortunately, he died a couple of months ago. He was a lawyer by training.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we scroll up on this document a little bit all the way to the top --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you -- something caught my eye here. Lieutenant-Colonel Dusan Novakovic, military police number -- can you enlarge the stamp? Only the stamp. 22230. This is not our military post number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what was your military post number?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first digit is a 4. Can we scroll up to the top or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can go back to the top and go to the first page, actually. You're saying the number is 4?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, 7001/46. Yes, this is our military post number. I don't know how one military post number can be stated up here and down there I saw a different number in the stamp. Well, I doubt the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's move away from this document. Now, sir, you did mention the presence of Colonel Peulic earlier today --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- and you are aware of the presence of his unit in your area since the month -- as of the month of March 1992?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that his unit had approximately a thousand soldiers and officers, would that agree with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nowhere close. Upon arriving at Kotor Varos municipality, and that was in March 1992, I think, that brigade was only 100 to 150 men strong. How it developed later, whether it was brought up to level or whatever, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Where did his brigade come from, sir?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a battalion. It wasn't a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So you're telling us that Colonel Peulic came with a battalion in the middle of March 1992 in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They arrived in Maslovare or Podborje in the valley of the Krusica river. Maslovare was where the command was. Maybe you meant the forward command post but that was a separate unit. The name of that unit was the 22nd Brigade. I know that it was established in the month of March and that at that time its strength was of the size of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Are you making a difference between the 22nd Brigade and Colonel Peulic's unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Are you saying it's the same unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to show you a chart of this brigade which is at tab 38, and that would be -- well, it's P1577. I see that it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It may be one of those documents that we don't really need to have under seal, Your Honours. I will refer, for the time being, if you'd like, we could not broadcast it until the decision has been issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, until we clarify the proper status.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this is a chart of the organisation of the 122nd Light Infantry Brigade between November 1991 and May 1992. You see the commander of the brigade. And to the left you can see the numbers, 35 officers, 32 non-commissioned officers, and 905 soldiers. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, because it was a different unit. I never had any personal contacts with that unit, so I'm not in a position to know anything about the organisation of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You are aware of the unit that was present in Maslovare; right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And did you know at the time that this unit was part of the brigade, of the 122nd Brigade, was it one of the units?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called that unit the 122nd Brigade -- I apologise, the 22nd Brigade, although it didn't even remotely look like a brigade because it did not have enough troops. However, people used to call it the 22nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right. And did you know that Commander Peulic was in charge of a wider region, not only Kotor Varos? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And, therefore, would you allow that this is one of the units of the brigade that was present in Maslovare? That what you saw in Maslovare was one of the units of the 22nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that. Let me tell you, we called that unit the 22nd Brigade. I don't know whether they had one or more. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Before I conclude for the day, sir, I do have one question in relation to a topic we discussed earlier today. Now, you remember when I was asking you about your willingness to meet with representatives of the Prosecution, you told us that you were informed that most people didn't meet both sides. You didn't tell me, though, who exactly told you that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke a number of people. I really can't tell you. Honestly, I can't. I spoke to some legal professionals. Because at my work, I co-operate with a number of lawyers and attorneys at law. I spoke to them, and they told me that it really didn't make much sense for me to talk to both sides. They told me: Either you are a Defence witness or a Prosecution witness. And that made perfect sense to me and it sounded perfectly acceptable, since I'm not a legal professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And when the investigators of Mr. Zupljanin asked you the question, did you also ask them whether it was usual to do -- to meet both sides?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position had already been formed. I had my mind set already and my answer was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Hang on a second. You're telling us that you had already made up your mind even before the question was asked?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The team asked me first, and then I said I would give it a thought and that either on the following day or the day after I would get back to them. Then I spoke to all those people and they told me that it didn't make much sense. I accepted that logic as my own and that's how I responded. I don't see how all that could be a sin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not saying that it is a sin, sir. I'm just trying to establish exactly who gave you this advice. Now, let me just get back here for a second. Now, you told us this morning, and I quote that when you were met by the investigators "on that occasion they told me that the Prosecutor also wanted to talk to me. And I asked those people how customary was that" --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- "to talk to both sides." Now, what I'm asking you now is when the investigators or whoever it is that asked you the question, you said: I asked those people how customary was that. Who are those people? Did you ask immediately the people asking you?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look here. I may have spoken rather hastily. Mr. Vukelic got in touch with me and told me what he did. When we spoke about that I consulted him as well and he told me that it would be entirely up to me. And then I consulted some other lawyers, and after that I made up my mind. He actually called me twice on the phone to ask me what my decision with this regard was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And when Mr. Vukelic -- when you gave your answer to Mr. Vukelic, did he ask you the reasons behind your decision?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD BUBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. He said, "It's up to you. It is going to be an -- entirely your decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll stop here for today, and as I noted I have a small application to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bubic, we are about to adjourn for the day but we have certain preliminary matters with which to deal. So the usher would escort you from the courtroom. We are to be -- we will rise -- we wouldn't rise immediately, but the usher would escort you from the courtroom and we would continue with your testimony tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Immediately, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, very well, now I've heard you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Next Friday being -- when is the witness scheduled to come? It would be the beginning of the next block, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. So if we have at least that much time in advance to prepare for the witness, we are saying that, at least, we will not be prejudiced by receiving a last-minute proofing note. Clearly Mr. Krgovic is in a position to meet with the witness next week and is in a position to provide us with a proofing note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, is that too onerous an obligation on you and your team?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid I can't speak without Mr. Krgovic. He already spoke to you with this regard earlier this morning. But can we go into private session just briefly for the rest of my submission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Aleksic, when do you expect the witness to arrive in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we are talking about SZ-007, he's supposed to testify on the 5th of December, the next time we sit. Witness SZ-022 is supposed to arrive later this afternoon. This is SZ-020, I apologise, he is either arriving -- he is either on his way or he has arrived already. My colleague Mr. Krgovic is proofing him, and the proofing notes, as far as I understood Mr. Krgovic earlier this morning, will be provided later this afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. We are not talking about the next witness. We are talking about the one for the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't believe that he will be in The Hague before the 2nd or the 3rd December. I really don't know. But it's not logical for the witness to arrive much sooner. Witnesses normally arrive two or three days before they're supposed to appear in court, in this case on the 2nd or the 3rd of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'll tell you what is a part of our thinking, Mr. Aleksic, that the arrangements that you have in place between the attorneys and the investigators that the relevant interviews can be conducted before they come to The Hague so you don't have to -- so we aren't faced with, for instance, what happened this week, where it's only when the witness comes in, he's interviewed, and the surprises come up, and we get the predictable complaints, rulings having to be made, so that the -- today is Wednesday ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we would require the proofing note to be provided not on the Friday that Mr. Demirdjian's asked for, but on the Wednesday of the following week, that is, the week preceding the witness's scheduled appearance before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we were informed by Mr. Krgovic that he will see this witness next week, so he is in a position to provide the proofing note by Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're not unmindful of what you have said, Mr. Demirdjian, but all things considered we think that Wednesday, the 4th -- the 30th - thank you - the 30th of November is reasonable in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Five days before the witness testifies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So if there is nothing else, we take the adjournment to reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of November, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
